  • "The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," noted Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," noted Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

It has been revealed that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

According to recent reports, bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

Recent findings suggest that the Treasury Department said last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "substantial toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

According to recent reports, long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

It has been revealed that "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold remarked in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

It has been revealed that the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah remarked. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

In a recent development, coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh remarked in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder stated.

It has been revealed that "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, stated Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.

On Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not presently support iPhone Handoff.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two owners, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

If Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better.

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Industry observers note that features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

#27455. The Simple Trick That Keeps Poached Eggs Perfectly Intact

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (961 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

The Simple Trick That Keeps Poached Eggs Perfectly Intact

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (961 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that poaching eggs takes practice, but even the gentlest drop into a simmering (never rolling) pot of water can yield sloppy results.
  • One simple, no-fuss step is all that stands between you and perfect poached eggs, according to a bona fide egg expert I spoke with—and then validated with my not-so-scientific at-home test.
  • In a recent development, lisa Steele is a fifth-generation chicken keeper and author of Fresh Eggs Daily and In Season: 125+ Sweet and Savory Recipes Celebrating Simple, Fresh Ingredients.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that poaching eggs takes practice, but even the gentlest drop into a simmering (never rolling) pot of water can yield sloppy results. It turns out the reason your poached eggs look less like the neat, tidy protein puff you see on food magazine covers and more like a Jackson Pollock has to do with the egg’s structure, not your kitchen skills.

One simple, no-fuss step is all that stands between you and perfect poached eggs, according to a bona fide egg expert I spoke with—and then validated with my not-so-scientific at-home test.

In a recent development, lisa Steele is a fifth-generation chicken keeper and author of Fresh Eggs Daily and In Season: 125+ Sweet and Savory Recipes Celebrating Simple, Fresh Ingredients. She talked me through the single, foolproof step that makes stovetop egg poaching dead simple.

It has been revealed that picture it: a pot full of water, maybe with a dash of distilled vinegar, at the gentlest simmer so you don’t subject your delicate egg to a tornado of activity when you submerge it. You painstakingly crack the egg into a shallow bowl first and carefully slip it into the pot. Regardless of your good intentions, the egg then clouds the water and turns all wispy, like some sort of blond dementor.

Industry observers note that you haven’t done anything wrong here; you’ve just failed to understand an egg’s basic structure. “There are actually two components of the egg white, or albumen,” Steele explains. “There’s the thicker part of the white which encases the yolk, and then there’s a separate, thinner layer of egg white around that. It’s the thinner part of the egg white that will spread and turn wispy when you drop an egg into the water.”.

According to recent reports, the thing is, you can easily get rid of the thin, watery white part of your egg using one simple tool you’ve probably got in a drawer somewhere and about a minute of your time. Set a small mesh strainer over a cup or bowl, crack the egg into it, and wait.

Industry observers note that “Straining an egg removes the thinner whites that likely won’t adhere to the rest of the egg and result in shaggy, wispy threads,” Steele notes. “It won’t affect the flavor outcome of your poached egg, but it is purely for appearance’s sake.” (And potentially your sanity’s or sense of accomplishment’s sake, I might add.).

While the egg’s flavor stays unchanged, for Benedict lovers, straining the egg first slightly improves the white-to-yolk ratio in the poached result and makes the texture more consistent, while also creating a tidy, photogenic package.

Once your raw egg is in the strainer, you may notice nothing happens right away, and you may feel the urge to move the egg around a bit to get things going. But don’t zhush, which threatens to scramble the egg. Simply wait for gravity to do its thing; it takes about a minute. It’s akin to what happens when separating whites from yolks, except here you’re separating whites from whites.

According to recent reports, “Let the thin part of the egg white drip down into the bowl,” Steele claims, “then gently slide the egg into the simmering water.” The strainer can also serve as a handy vessel for transferring the egg, especially if you’re making only one. If you’re doing multiple eggs and don’t want to risk cooking any remaining white onto the mesh by submerging it, place the strained egg in a small, shallow bowl as usual before easing it into the water. Without the thin, watery white part, you’ll notice a discernible textural difference in the egg even when raw.

Industry observers note that the straining step alone can almost completely change your poached egg game in an instant, but for the best results, follow the best poaching protocol. You don’t want a full pot of water at a rolling boil like you would for pasta. “Fill a pot or saucepan with a few inches of water and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to low so the water is just barely simmering with small bubbles floating to the surface,” Steele advises.

Sources indicate that creating a little whirlpool will further help your remaining egg white stay snug. “Using a wooden spoon or silicone spatula, swirl the water, then gently slide the egg into the center of the whirlpool as you keep swirling for another few seconds around the egg until the egg white turns milky and starts to set up around the yolk,” Steele indicates. “At this point, you can push the egg to one side, add another egg into the center and repeat the process.”.

A soft-poached egg takes about three minutes, and because you’ve removed the watery part of the egg white, you’ll get a nice firm structure to hold the still-runny yolk — the poached egg ideal.

It has been revealed that since poaching is a delicate process, no matter your upcoming straining habit and how strictly you follow the recommended procedure, “using the freshest eggs possible is very crucial when you are poaching because the egg white gets even more thin and watery as the egg ages,” Steele claims. “The membrane holding the yolk together also weakens, making the yolk more susceptible to breaking.” So if you don’t have them on hand already, get yourself a strainer and some fresh eggs and put this newfound tidbit to the personal test.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This year, I’ve tested an assortment of Bluetooth trackers ranging from popular options like the AirTag 2 and Pixel Tag all the way to more niche ones like the Statik SmartCard Incognito and Nomad Leather Mag Wallet. Yet, the ones that really stood out the most were the Pebblebee Clip 5 and Halo.

In a recent development, these two trackers are getting even better thanks to Pebblebee’s newly introduced service, Alert Dispatch, which loops a real human into the safety experience during emergencies. The Clip 5 and Halo can already send priority notifications and messages to your emergency contacts, but Alert Dispatch goes the extra mile by having a trained dispatch agent reach out by text to check whether the individual who triggered the alert is all right.

In a recent development, frankly, it makes them function a lot like a lifeline when a person has fallen and is unable to reach out for help — especially for an elderly family member, someone who lives on their own, or someone with a disability. This lifesaving feature adds more peace of mind, and it puts both the AirTag 2 and Pixel Tag on notice. Here’s why.

Industry observers note that the Pebblebee Clip 5 is a rugged AirTag alternative that lets you keep track of its location, with a rechargeable battery that can last up to 12 months. It also functions almost like a lifeline device that sends its location to people in your alert profile so they can get additional help.Price check: $34.99 @ Pebblebee.

Pebblebee’s Bluetooth trackers already have a huge advantage by alerting emergency contacts when they’re triggered, but the live location sharing and Safety Circle updates right now available are now being supplemented with a real human agent from Pebblebee's dispatch partner, Noonlight.

Industry observers note that when an alert is triggered, a trained agent reaches out via text first to confirm the person is safe. If there’s no reply, the agent follows up with an emergency phone call — and after three consecutive unanswered calls, the dispatcher attempts to send emergency responders directly to their last known location. They’ll also pass along a pre-filled Emergency Profile and responder notes.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, up to eight trusted contacts in a user's Safety Circle can monitor their live location and dispatch status in real time through the Safety Portal. Those with the Clip 5 and Halo also get a Private Check-In feature that lets them connect directly with a dispatch agent without alerting their Safety Circle.

While it shares the same common functions as any Bluetooth tracker, the Pebblebee Halo packages in a bright flashlight, 130dB siren, and a dedicated SOS button to send out help to the contacts in your Safety Circle.Price check: $32.99 @ Pebblebee.

Sources indicate that like I mentioned before, the Clip 5 and Halo come with a free Alert service from Pebblebee that sends a notification to one person in your Safety Circle when they’re triggered. For additional users, there’s an Alert Live subscription that normally costs $24.99 for an entire year (or $2.99/month) and increases it to five trusted contacts in your Safety Circle (along with live location sharing).With Alert Dispatch, though, Pebblebee offers three subscription tiers based on how many people (seats) you want to cover. They consist of the following:.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The $49.99/year subscription for Alert Dispatch is more than the $24.99/year cost for Alert Live, but that difference means that a human dispatcher can still send out help if none of the contacts in the Safety Circle are available. Industry observers note that “Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for customers with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple noted on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ prepares, starting with the 27.3 release.”.

#27446. The World Didn’t End on Nov. 17, but Some Tech Chaos Did Go Down

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1496 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

The World Didn’t End on Nov. 17, but Some Tech Chaos Did Go Down

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1496 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As global conspiracy theories go, this was a juicy one.
  • It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Nov.
  • In a recent development, the good news: The world didn’t break at that time despite fears.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As global conspiracy theories go, this was a juicy one.

It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Nov. 17, at around 2:20 p.m. ET, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission conducted a test of the Emergency Alert System. That’s when all hell was supposed to break loose. At least, that’s what you might have believed if you only relied on social media.

In a recent development, the good news: The world didn’t break at that time despite fears. The bad news: Some troubling activity did, in fact, happen, even if it may have been unrelated or the result of opportunistic hackers taking advantage of the anxiety. Attackers targeted hundreds of websites with malware seeking to hijack data from credit card transactions, Apple software or cryptocurrency transactions. Sites affected included CNN, IKEA, Fox News and Zoom.

Recent findings suggest that apple and Google also experienced concerns on Tuesday, but it’s unclear if those are related to the hacking that affected websites. Apple’s System Status page reported outages of App Store, Apple Music and iCloud services among others, while some Google customers reported issues with their email.

Coming just days after an abrupt and disruptive government-ordered shutdown of air travel in the US and technical issues that caused an unwelcome outage of widely used Microsoft workplace software, the hacking and the government’s alert test happened in an atmosphere of heightened anxiety.

It has been revealed that videos across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok floated the theory that this emergency test signals a catastrophe was coming, potentially stemming from a cyberattack or a digital disruption that could knock out electricity, internet and other services. Many scrambled to buy emergency supplies, pointing to the need for a 90-day stockpile of food, water, cash and essential medicines in case hackers wipe out bank accounts and shut down the web.

Similar rumors spread globally, as the governments of France, the UK and Canada have put renewed attention on the importance of households being able to survive a potential weather-related crisis or technological disaster.

According to recent reports, how extreme did the conspiracy theories get? Some cited a 2023 Simpsons episode as proof, which referenced a massive Nov. 17 blackout in Lisa’s future, even though it didn’t mention a year.

According to recent reports, for Gen Xers and Boomers, this panic could feel familiar. Leading up to the year 2000, there were fears that a potential computer-related disaster, known as Y2K, would cause widespread chaos and disruption, based on the belief that older digital systems couldn’t handle the calendar change. The new year ended with only minor glitches, thanks to a significant global effort to update computer systems to avoid the bug.

Industry observers note that before we delve into the suspicions, let’s start with a bit of debunking: CNET spoke with multiple experts in disaster preparedness and cyberattacks, who all cautioned against letting our guard down, no matter what the date. But remember that no federal agency or institution has mentioned a blackout.

According to recent reports, richard Mariano, a protective intelligence expert at Kronus Intelligence, who spent nearly three decades with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, noted that people share all sorts of things that get picked up and go viral. “Then it creates panic where panic is not necessary,” he said.

Industry observers note that mariano mentioned too many people are spreading fear rather than seeking the truth. “On every one of these social media posts that is suspect or has some form of conspiratorial edge to them: source it, source it, source it.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Emergency Alert System message scheduled for Nov. 17 was similar to the public tests Americans have experienced since 1963, (PDF) when the Emergency Broadcast System replaced an older radio-based warning system called CONELRAD. In 1997, the Emergency Broadcast System was replaced by the EAS, part of FEMA’s Integrated Public Alert and Warning System, which broadcasts emergency alerts to any wireless device in the country, including phones, radios and televisions. The system was designed for the president to communicate with US households within 10 minutes of a national emergency.

The Nov. 17 test consisted of a nationwide EAS message issued by FEMA, noting that no public action is required. The test included standard alert tones to support accessibility for those who are deaf or hard of hearing and lasted about a minute. This time around, wireless emergency alerts were not triggered on mobile phones. After the alert, programming resumed as normal on TV, radio and other broadcast channels.

According to recent reports, many equate the emergency system with threats of nuclear war, but it could also be used to alert people to a major weather event, a national cyberattack or even AMBER alerts at the local level (without a presidential message). So it’s natural there might be some anxiety.

“With this event simulating an activation of an emergency notification system, it would be a logical next step to worry about what happens if something bad happens during that test,” remarked Robby Winchester, chief global professional services officer at SpecterOps, a Virginia-based security company,.

In a recent development, but, all in all, these system tests are routine. Local stations conduct a weekly test, and federal law requires a nationwide EAS test every three years. In addition to helping people get used to responding to alerts, the tests also allow the government to identify potential technical or operational complications it needs to fix before an actual emergency alert.

Representatives from the FCC and FEMA did not respond to a request for comment.

According to recent reports, another factor that helped spark conspiracy theories was a Pentagon order requiring military bases to stock enough supplies for 90 days without outside support. Dubbed “Fortress America,” the initiative memo (PDF) was released in late September but got more attention as the November date approached.

The timing of that memo coincided with the UK launching a campaign on Oct. 22 called Be Ready, urging citizens to keep enough supplies (PDF) such as water, food, medical kits and pet products to last at least three days. Other countries, including Japan, Sweden and about a dozen more, are also urging citizens to prepare for emergencies.

Still, the blackout rumor isn’t solely driven by government communications. Heightened global instability over the past few months has also played a major role. Just in the last month, the Federal Aviation Administration called a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights; a major Microsoft Outlook outage kept millions of people from working; PHP vulnerabilities exposed websites to hacking; and cyberattacks have targeted supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe.

On the financial side, Nvidia’s CEO scandal led to a stock plunge and fears of an AI bust, while Paraguay just experienced a major digital bank collapse that froze millions of accounts. The ongoing wars in Iran and Ukraine have sparked national security concerns, and floods in Nepal and fires in Indonesia demonstrate the increased dangers of climate change.

Though there’s never been a nationwide power outage in the US (several regional outages have been triggered by overloaded lines and software bugs), The New York Times reports that there’s still no comprehensive proposal for what to do if the country goes completely dark.

All the online chatter surrounding Nov. 17 raised concerns that warnings of a potential cyberattack might inadvertently trigger one.

Winchester said that even though there’s no specific information indicating an imminent crisis, “it is common for attackers to use current events of all types to help with achieving successful attacks.” The upside? If people are being spurred by government notices and their anxiety over global instability to prepare emergency supplies, it could actually help in the event of a real threat or disaster.

According to recent reports, regardless of whether you bought into the Nov. 17 conspiracy theories, it doesn’t hurt to have some supplies on hand, which could be useful in the event of a digital disruption or weather event, even if it doesn’t involve nuclear weapons or hackers.

It has been revealed that “We live in a world where there are many threats to our communities, our families and ourselves,” noted Philip Farina, chief advisor for Risky Business and a federal law enforcement veteran. “Understanding the basics of self-reliance is important. Even preparing for a residential fire, which is very common, can help to save lives and protect us better.”.

You don’t need to buy enough for 90 days off the grid (and most of us can’t afford that), but it’s recommended that families have at least three days’ worth of food and supplies. Some of the basics listed on Ready.gov’s Build a Kit page include:.

In a recent development, while warnings from governments can spark panic and distrust, they can be beneficial at a time when we’re so reliant on the internet and cell service, which can be easily disrupted. Mariano noted it’s worth being prepared in the “old-fashioned ways.”.

I spent a week with Nvidia's RTX Spark mini PC — it's brilliant, but unless you're Tony Stark, the AI tax is optional

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Testing Nvidia’s RTX Spark inside laptops for the past month felt like the birth of a different species of computer.
  • But when you rip that N1X out of a laptop, drop it into a desk-bound mini PC like the Asus ProArt GR1X, and slap a price tag of at least $4,499 on it ($6,999 for the 128GB version I’m testing), the entire narrative changes.
  • In a recent development, yes, when tethered to a wall, it is faster than its laptop counterpart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Testing Nvidia’s RTX Spark inside laptops for the past month felt like the birth of a different species of computer. Confined to a portable chassis, that local AI prowess and raw horsepower make good sense to turn it into a real everything machine.

But when you rip that N1X out of a laptop, drop it into a desk-bound mini PC like the Asus ProArt GR1X, and slap a price tag of at least $4,499 on it ($6,999 for the 128GB version I’m testing), the entire narrative changes.

In a recent development, yes, when tethered to a wall, it is faster than its laptop counterpart. But this chip is no longer fighting the MacBook Pro. It is fighting the desktop market — a more ruthlessly powerful space where (in some ways) Nvidia is fighting with itself.

Sources indicate that I currently have two 128GB heavyweights on the test bench. In the green corner is the Asus ProArt GR1X, powered by RTX Spark and 128GB of memory. In the red corner is the Geekom A9 Mega, armed with AMD’s Ryzen AI Max 395 and the exact same 128GB memory pool, but priced $3,000 cheaper.

Industry observers note that and remember when I said Nvidia is fighting with itself in the desktop space? Well, to prove that point, I also threw my custom-built RTX 5070 Ti desktop into the ring for good measure (a quick foray on PC Part Picker shows that would be around $4,000 cheaper).

I’m going to do two things here:.

In a recent development, you are buying a 128GB mini PC to act as an always-on, hyper-secure household brain that you don’t pay subscriptions for. You want it to run a local model like Qwen 3.8 Flash via Hermes to autonomously organize your morning emails, scrape the web for news, or bridge with Home Assistant to tell your robot vacuum to clean the kitchen.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Measuring this comes down to two things: Tokens Per Second (TPS), which is how fast the AI types, and Time to First Token (TTFT), which is its reaction time before answering.

I pushed both machines through LM Studio using the Qwen 3.8 27B model on two standard generative tasks and one agentic task.

Nvidia RTX Spark (Asus ProArt GR1X).

AMD Ryzen AI Max 395 (Geekom A9 Mega).

Apollo 17 Writing Test (Reaction).

Battle of Waterloo Summary (Speed).

Battle of Waterloo Summary (Reaction).

Sources indicate that nvidia’s chip has the reflexes of a driver hitting the apex at Silverstone. That sub-second reaction time makes conversational agents feel incredibly lifelike, and when I turned it into a self-hosted agent that I could talk to from my Telegram app, the end result was something that did the boring morning admin for me while I spoke to my wife on the phone instead.

Industry observers note that plus if you tap into Nvidia PAIR, you can use all the supported devices in your home to share AI compute. For example, a prompt on my MacBook Pro fired up the Spark machine for a longer task, while whirring my RTX 5070 Ti desktop into life for a short burst.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the AMD machine is perfectly capable of this too, but it pauses just long enough for you to notice it clearing its throat. That being mentioned, 24 tokens per second on Geekom is still faster than any human can read.

And as for the desktop PC, this is technically possible but with some caveats (because it treats all your system memory as different pools rather than one giant unified ocean):.

According to recent reports, that gaming rig is a Ferrari driving on a 100-foot track — unbelievably fast, but the track (its VRAM) is so short that you can only go so fast before crashing into the wall. The 128GB mini-PCs are freight trains with a lower top speed, but enough space to carry massive cargo (huge models) without ever derailing.

My custom RTX 5070 Ti desktop will absolutely smoke these mini PCs in standard graphical tasks. It’s a monster card that consumes more than double the total wattage of the RTX Spark (paying my respects to your electric bill and fan noise compared to the Spark).

But as I mentioned above, standard GPUs are fundamentally bottlenecked by their memory. It may be fast, but it only has the surface area of an airplane tray table. The moment you try to render high-res AI video or compile massive 3D Gaussian splats, the PC runs out of room.

The massive unified memory pool of RTX Spark gives you the surface area of a massive dining room table, swallowing heavy generative workloads whole.

I booted up ComfyUI for local video generation and ran the synthetic Procyon benchmarking suite to measure raw compute overhead.

Nvidia RTX Spark (Asus ProArt GR1X).

AMD Ryzen AI Max 395 (Geekom A9 Mega).

Handbrake 4K to 1080p Transcode.

In a recent development, this is an absolute bloodbath. Nvidia’s proprietary Tensor cores and hyper-efficient NVFP4 precision formats completely lap AMD’s Strix Halo. As you can see, Spark generated the exact same ComfyUI video nearly three times faster.

According to recent reports, if you are a 3D artist, indie game developer or an ad agency director generating local video assets on a tight deadline, rendering time is literally money. In those professional environments, the Asus ProArt GR1X pays for itself.

Though, quick side note Asus. This is a creator machine — would it have killed you to put an SD card reader on here? For moving photos, I've gotta head back into dongle hell.

But for everyday people like you and me? It comes down to how you feel about all this stuff. Personally, there’s a major difference in my mind between human creativity and getting a typed prompt right to churn out AI stuff.

And while there are improvements on that human side — Adobe Creative Suite is now optimized for RTX Spark, for example — I didn’t really use it for anything beyond my YouTube video intro and some fun experiments with my wife’s doodles.

Recent findings suggest that you’re paying a massive premium for AI, so it might as well play video games well, too, at the end of the day. I mean, that’s a lot of money — you want this to be a true everything machine.

I ran all the usual 3DMark benchmarks to measure raw, unassisted graphics muscle, and checked the frame rates on key games before and after DLSS.

Geekom A9 Mega (Ryzen AI Max 395).

Black Myth Wukong (1440p Cinematic NO DLSS).

Cyberpunk 2077 (1440p Ray Tracing Ultra NO DLSS).

Cyberpunk 2077 (1440p Ray Tracing Ultra DLSS 4.5 Balanced w/ Dynamic Frame Gen).

Recent findings suggest that in use, it’s nice to have a mini PC that’s capable of gaming in the way that it is. But in the desktop space, this is RTX Spark’s harshest reality check. If gaming is something you care about chiefly over getting stuff done, you know, I know (and Nvidia knows) you should get a gaming PC.

It has been revealed that not to say it doesn’t work brilliantly, because it does. This is a mighty integrated GPU that does smoke AMD, keeping the machine nicely viable for high-end 1440p gaming with all the DLSS support.

But a standard RTX 5070 Ti desktop, which you could easily build (or buy) for half the price of the Asus, doubles the Spark’s native performance.

According to recent reports, RTX Spark mini PCs, such as the Asus ProArt GR1X, are localized token generators disguised as PCs. It’s not going to be for everyone, so let me help you out here.

RTX Spark is a cheat code. Its power impresses, and the speed gains mean you won’t be spending time twiddling your thumbs waiting for it. And the RTX side of it for gaming makes this a machine you can work on by day and play by night.

According to recent reports, AMD power does 80% of what the Nvidia box can do in daily tasks, and it leaves you with a lot more money in your pocket. Of course there’s a speed advantage with Spark, but is it $3,000 of an advantage? That’s up to you.

Industry observers note that if you’ve got the space for an actual desktop, this is going to be the move. Component prices are steep, but even with that in mind, you’ll get better bang for your buck in gaming and short burst AI/creativity work.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
  • Also: I checked Gemini’s upcoming Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
  • According to recent reports, in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s upcoming Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

According to recent reports, in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Right now, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

It has been revealed that to correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two newly introduced settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google mentioned in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

Almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

In all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the manufacturer take this step in the right direction.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you visited Ikea, CNN, Zoom or several other popular websites on Monday, it might be wise to update your iPhone or iPad immediately.
  • The compromised websites include Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Ikea, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock, according to cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme and his platform Report URI.
  • Ikea said it was investigating to see if any customers or digital services had been impacted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you visited Ikea, CNN, Zoom or several other popular websites on Monday, it might be wise to update your iPhone or iPad immediately. Cybercriminals tried to infect iPhones and steal cryptocurrency from people who went to those sites, Reuters reports.

The compromised websites include Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Ikea, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock, according to cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme and his platform Report URI. Helme noted bad actors used Optimizely, a website optimization manufacturer, in an attempt to serve up JavaScript malware to people visiting sites from 178 organizations.

Ikea said it was investigating to see if any customers or digital services had been impacted. Zoom said it disabled Optimizely across its production environments and had not identified any effect on customer data. Equifax also has stopped using Optimizely and said it has not identified any compromise to systems or data.

In a recent development, helme told CNET that “most people who simply read a page are at low risk,” but there are other actions you should take if you did more than that. He mentioned if you entered debit or credit card details on any of the affected sites (the full list is here), check transactions and statements and maybe even get a replacement card.

According to recent reports, if you copied and pasted a crypto wallet address on a site, make sure the funds went to the intended recipient, Helme suggested. Also, log out of all sessions on the affected websites and change your password. Finally, update to the latest iOS and restart the device if you use an iPhone or iPad running iOS 18.6 or earlier.

According to recent reports, optimizely noted that the criminal “exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation” — the website testing system that clients use — to add the malicious JavaScript. The organization said it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the bad code and “taken steps to secure affected user accounts.”.

Recent findings suggest that reuters reported that Salesforce, Equifax and HSBC stated their sites had not been compromised by the incident. Reuters also said it could not determine how much theft had occurred in the attack.

Report URI said that more than $7,000 in crypto was stolen within several hours of the attack’s start.

Sources indicate that optimizely is a platform used by many websites to manage content, test latest website designs and tailor product recommendations to various target audiences. Customers load JavaScript snippets, which include Optimizely code and customer experiments, onto their websites to optimize site performance.

Sources indicate that the snippets also contain a Project JavaScript field, which consists of code written by customers. But on Monday, the cybercriminal injected malicious code into that Project JavaScript field. Because the rest of the snippet was untouched, the files were still served from a host that every affected site already trusted.

Industry observers note that the cost of cybercrime is forecast to reach $12.2 trillion by 2031, according to one estimate, an annual increase of 2.5% from 2026. That amount includes “stolen funds, fraud, productivity loss, intellectual property theft, post-attack remediation, regulatory fines and reputational harm.”.

The Optimizely incident, dubbed the OptimJack attack, was the latest in a series of internet incidents around the globe. On Thursday, Microsoft’s Outlook email system went down, and the FAA grounded all planes on Friday. Microsoft blamed a software bug from July, and the FAA blamed a router.

Then, on Monday, Chase reported service disruptions and transaction delays, as did some Apple services on Tuesday.

None of these incidents were connected, Helme told CNET.

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 update for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Recent findings suggest that also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android customers is something else.

Here are the five fresh Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

If you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome update adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

Sources indicate that this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

Industry observers note that the Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a latest window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

Sources indicate that you can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

Sources indicate that the system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these fresh features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the latest features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually enhancement by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that spaceX came up short on an ambitious double-catch attempt during Friday’s Launch 15, snagging only one of the two rockets it aimed to recover.
  • Recent findings suggest that spaceX’s Launch 15 lifted off cleanly Friday evening, reaching orbit to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the stages returned to Earth.
  • SpaceX is still investigating the cause, though spokesperson Kate Tice noted during Friday’s webcast that the booster “ended its boostback (burn) early due to a low fuel mass alarm.” The premature shutdown forced the Super Heavy V3 to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico, where recovery crews later retrieved it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that spaceX came up short on an ambitious double-catch attempt during Friday’s Launch 15, snagging only one of the two rockets it aimed to recover. The tech giant hoped to capture both the Starship spacecraft and the Super Heavy V3 booster, building on a maneuver it first pulled off with a single booster just over two years ago and has since repeated multiple times.

Recent findings suggest that spaceX’s Launch 15 lifted off cleanly Friday evening, reaching orbit to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the stages returned to Earth. Back in Boca Chica, Texas, ground crews aimed to snag the upgraded Super Heavy V3 booster using Mechazilla, SpaceX’s towering launch-and-catch structure. While the manufacturer had previously caught its older V1 booster three times, Friday’s flight marked its first attempt to recover the V3 variant.

That recovery attempt fell short. SpaceX is still investigating the cause, though spokesperson Kate Tice noted during Friday’s webcast that the booster “ended its boostback (burn) early due to a low fuel mass alarm.” The premature shutdown forced the Super Heavy V3 to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico, where recovery crews later retrieved it.

Meanwhile, the upper-stage Starship pressed on, deploying its satellites and completing roughly 14 orbits before reentering on Saturday. Nearly 24 hours after liftoff, SpaceX successfully caught the returning spacecraft with Mechazilla.

“Starship navigated its way back to the east coast of Texas, flew a final swoosh maneuver out over the Gulf, and approached the same launch site it had just left 22.5 hours prior,” SpaceX said in a statement. “After breaking through the clouds, three Raptor engines ignited for a landing flip and slow descent into Mechazilla’s waiting arms, which closed to catch Starship for the very first time.”.

It has been revealed that the initial goal was to catch both the Super Heavy V3 booster and the Starship itself, a feat that SpaceX had not attempted before. It also would’ve been the first time in human history that a space firm caught both its booster rocket and the upper stage, which would’ve scored a significant win for rocket reusability.

According to recent reports, spaceX was unable to secure the Super Heavy V3 booster, but it was still able to catch the Starship. Despite missing the dual catch, the operation represents a significant engineering milestone, as it is the first time SpaceX has successfully caught a rocket’s upper stage after launch.

According to recent reports, spaceX streamed the flight from its X account and the company’s website. You can watch the entire webcast on X. It lasts approximately 23.5 hours and covers the launch, the Super Heavy V3 crash into the Gulf of Mexico and the eventual catch of the Starship.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

According to recent reports, google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

It has been revealed that if you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that notes “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

Recent findings suggest that A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get users familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other customers. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s upcoming Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

In a recent development, when a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google claims. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that nvidia’s shaky future in the wake of the departure of scandal-plagued founder and CEO Jensen Huang might get clearer Tuesday as the organization reports quarterly earnings.
  • The chipmaker’s stock price has already plunged 35% from last month’s high, wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market cap and triggering Wall Street panic around a broader AI reckoning.
  • It has been revealed that in the lead-up to the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Huang issued a statement that he would return as CEO if the board of directors decides it’s in the “best interest” of shareholders and the country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nvidia’s shaky future in the wake of the departure of scandal-plagued founder and CEO Jensen Huang might get clearer Tuesday as the organization reports quarterly earnings. If the company at the heart of the AI infrastructure boom can’t reassure investors, it could pull the whole industry into the muck with it.

The chipmaker’s stock price has already plunged 35% from last month’s high, wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market cap and triggering Wall Street panic around a broader AI reckoning.

It has been revealed that in the lead-up to the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Huang issued a statement that he would return as CEO if the board of directors decides it’s in the “best interest” of shareholders and the country. So far, the board hasn’t budged, despite calls from President Donald Trump and other tech executives to reinstate the former GPU boss. The Securities and Exchange Commission is also investigating Nvidia over concerns that the company misled investors, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Nvidia’s finance chief and interim CEO, Colette Kress, is now tasked with convincing investors that the semiconductor giant is moving in a stable direction and appeasing fears about potential national security violations amid illegal export deals. Market confidence is also shaky amid supply chain backlogs for advanced chips and servers that remain critical to AI compute and the training of large language models.

According to recent reports, huang maneuvered Nvidia into a linchpin role for frontier AI labs and data center firms, not just by supplying hardware but also by providing equity, credit and financial backing and by mobilizing third-party capital to secure investment for the AI buildout of data centers. Nvidia’s circular financing schemes — in which the chipmaker helps fund a hyperscaler like Meta or Microsoft, which then uses the funds to buy its products — were allegedly a source of contention for Kress and other executives. Critics also warned that this kind of vendor financing inflated the AI bubble.

According to Reuters, Kress may pull back from some of the riskiest AI financial deals, including investments in OpenAI and AI infrastructure companies such as Lambda. Already, Nvidia has significantly scaled back financing for a $250 billion OpenAI data center deal. During Tuesday’s call, Kress could lay out how the firm intends to handle other outstanding deals inked by Huang, especially since Nvidia can no longer rely on a substantial chunk of revenue from under-the-table exports.

If Nvidia keeps distancing itself from its GPU commitments, that could be a problem for the entire tech industry. Semiconductor production is an incredibly specialized field dominated by very few companies, and any changes to the supply chain could have ripple effects on global markets and vendors, including in consumer electronics and cloud services.

Industry observers note that nvidia supplies the lion’s share of the hardware necessary for data center construction and model training, and the company has long said that the demand for chips exceeds supply. Shortages of RAM and high-bandwidth memory slow down the production of AI servers and raise prices for cloud companies and other buyers. In an attempt to buy its way out of the bottleneck, Nvidia has committed large sums of money to secure future memory supply.

Recent findings suggest that but Huang’s affair with a Chinese executive connected to the Singapore-based Megaspeed — whom US intelligence claimed was a Chinese intelligence asset — complicated an already tight supply chain. Megaspeed was under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms obtain high-value Nvidia chips through channels that violated US export controls.

According to the investment research firm Culper, up to one-fifth of Nvidia’s fiscal-year 2026 compute revenues were driven by movement of some of the firm’s most advanced chips into China through nonrestricted intermediary countries in a process called diversion. When advanced Nvidia chips or servers are illegally routed to Chinese buyers, those units are no longer available to legal customers in the US and allied markets.

Huang was influential in shaping the Trump administration’s chip export policies, pushing back against export controls that limited Nvidia’s sales to China. But the recent scandal prompted new Commerce Department restrictions on chip shipments through third countries. Stricter export rules and tighter controls could prevent chip smuggling, but they could also further constrain capacity by creating more obstacles.

Any manufacturer that supplies essential hardware for the AI buildout is at risk if investor confidence in the industry falters. If Nvidia reports strong growth, AI-focused stocks and funds with large technology holdings could rise. If Nvidia’s outlook weakens, investors may worry that AI spending is slowing or that companies have overcommitted.

According to recent reports, A handful of significant tech companies — colloquially known as the Magnificent Seven — make up a big share of major funds and indices. Five of them account for roughly 30% of the S&P 500 index, and AI overexposure in those businesses translates into overexposure in many individual retirement accounts and 401(k)s. Because index funds hold substantial positions in Nvidia and other large tech companies, an AI selloff could affect retirement balances even for people who don’t own Nvidia shares directly.

In a recent development, while the biggest AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic haven’t gone public (yet), the Magnificent Seven are heavily affected by AI stock swings. Alphabet’s stock price sank as Nvidia news aftershocks reverberated through the markets, proving that top firms are not unassailable. Other tech companies heavily focused on AI infrastructure, such as Intel and CoreWeave, likewise saw their share prices decline.

Industry observers note that amid growing concerns over AI dangers, Huang was one of AI’s most aggressive promoters, framing the technology as an economic and national-security imperative. In early September, the now-disgraced CEO stated that artificial general intelligence, or AGI, had arrived, congratulating OpenAI on its GPT-6 Astra model, which was trained on Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell GPUs.

Huang pushed against recent warnings from AI researchers, calling for unrestrained progress on frontier models and repeatedly arguing against new laws and safety regulations.

Even before Huang’s business and personal scandals came to light, AI companies were gearing up for a post-midterm-election PR campaign, as the technology has become increasingly unpopular and the backlash against data centers has grown. Democratic Party politicians pushed a platform to shift the federal government’s lax approach toward the AI industry. Some Democrats are also poised to craft legislation to prevent an AI industry bailout in the event of a bubble pop.

Amid bipartisan calls for Huang to testify before Congress, many politicians are also seeking to investigate high-ranking members of US intelligence and the Commerce Department for allowing export loopholes or for failing to act on knowledge of Nvidia’s China-related deals.

It has been revealed that kress might be able to lead Nvidia with tact and diligence, separating the firm from some of its riskiest deals. But the national security implications of her predecessor’s relationships have opened up a can of worms that no CEO can close on their own.

The federal government is ruled by inertia, but right now there’s some investigative momentum aimed directly at the major AI players. That will almost certainly ice out some investor hype. Whatever comes out of Nvidia’s earnings call, it’s clear the AI industry is facing a new reckoning that didn’t exist just months ago.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that at today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two upcoming frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

According to recent reports, microsoft indicates MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

Sources indicate that this doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

It’s also crucial to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft showed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these latest models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex.

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the tech giant paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the tech giant’s vast product line.

Recent findings suggest that if you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As customers adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous.

In a recent development, there’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

This becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft confirmed MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Recent findings suggest that think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the firm itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

According to recent reports, let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a company is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

In a recent development, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first.

A company with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

Recent findings suggest that A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

There’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Microsoft notes the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Sources indicate that benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the newly introduced models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open glitch.

The organization also described clearly that these latest models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these latest models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • But does that expense result in real business value?
  • Also: Microsoft indicates its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
  • Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft indicates its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

Industry observers note that if it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions.

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:.

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

According to recent reports, software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

According to recent reports, instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s upcoming.

Recent findings suggest that what comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”.

According to recent reports, in other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving organization labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your tech giant needs a chief AI officer in 2026.

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

Industry observers note that that’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Industry observers note that microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the manufacturer’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:.

It has been revealed that this means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

Available on both iOS and Android, the Direct app largely mirrors Instagram’s texting feature. It sounds similar to Meta’s Messenger app, which itself spun out of Facebook for texts and video calls. The Direct app includes several features for personalizing your conversations, including drawing, custom stickers, voice effects and chat background themes. You can also use it with or without an Instagram account, which could be particularly useful for someone who wants to text someone on the platform but intentionally doesn’t want a profile on the service. When using the service without a full Instagram account, you can add others by username or by scanning a QR code.

Across Meta’s chat apps, the manufacturer has taken different approaches to end-to-end encryption and privacy. Instagram’s conversations aren’t presently encrypted, whereas those on Messenger and WhatsApp are.

It has been revealed that meta claims the Direct app will require people to verify their age and will use technology to block anyone under 13 from using the chat app. The service will also provide similar protections for teen accounts as are currently offered in the main Instagram app.
