💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption.
  • During the keynote for the organization’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella declared Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
  • Also: Microsoft claims its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the organization’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella declared Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft claims its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several upcoming Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also revealed Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft remarked, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s fresh Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft remarked the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

Sources indicate that “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

The tech giant added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Right now in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft mentioned of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

Industry observers note that microsoft also revealed that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft unveiled a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

In a recent development, agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the firm’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft highlighted how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

According to recent reports, “It starts with a latest way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

According to recent reports, “Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft mentioned. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise intends.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An open-source AI tool designed to find security flaws is helping hackers launch cyberattacks.
  • The advisory was issued the same day communications problems prompted a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop and a day after a major Microsoft 365 outage began.
  • An FBI official told ABC News⁠ that Artex doesn’t appear to be connected to either incident or to other recent disruptions, including banking outages involving JPMorgan Chase.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An open-source AI tool designed to find security flaws is helping hackers launch cyberattacks. The FBI claims hackers are using Artex, an AI-powered security testing tool, to break into organizations worldwide. In an advisory on Friday, the agency said some attacks took less than 3 hours from selecting a target to gaining high-level access to its systems. Attackers have used Artex since at least August against banks, government agencies, technology companies and healthcare providers.

The advisory was issued the same day communications problems prompted a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop and a day after a major Microsoft 365 outage began. Microsoft attributed its disruption to technical problems, and the FAA claims it has found no indication of a cyberattack.

An FBI official told ABC News⁠ that Artex doesn’t appear to be connected to either incident or to other recent disruptions, including banking outages involving JPMorgan Chase.

The warning adds to concerns about the security risks posed by AI agents, which can carry out tasks with little human supervision.

According to recent reports, artex automates security tests that organizations use to uncover weaknesses. According to Microsoft’s analysis, its agents can examine defenses, exploit flaws and extract data. Attackers can use that automation to try several ways into a network simultaneously.

The FBI cited attacks against South Korean financial institutions that exposed the personal information of approximately 67,000 people. Microsoft warns that attackers breached over 2,250 organizations’ Microsoft 365 systems in a separate campaign, using stolen ConnectWise backup credentials alongside the Artex tool.

It has been revealed that because customers had already authorized the backup software, attackers could use its access without logging in as an individual user. Microsoft cautioned that a successful sign-in doesn’t necessarily mean data was accessed or stolen. The automated attacks could trigger security alerts, but their speed left defenders little time to respond.

It has been revealed that this FBI Cyber advisory on ARTEX was released last Friday, 11/13. It is not a new announcement, and the FBI has not issued any additional warning since. The guidance in the advisory remains current.We released this advisory last week because as we head to the end of the year,….

According to recent reports, amazon Web Services’ Nov. 13 research described another scheme: Stealing credentials for AI services, and then using that access to hunt for more credentials at someone else’s expense. Amazon Threat Intelligence uncovered the activity through decoy systems posing as AI services. It linked the campaigns to Artex with moderate confidence but couldn’t independently verify results the agents reported on systems outside its monitoring.

Amazon noted the attacks relied on default passwords, exposed login details and outdated software, all of which hackers can find and exploit faster with AI.

Recent findings suggest that artex’s developer removed the original GitHub repository in October after reports of abuse, but copies remain available, the FBI remarked. The agency recommends limiting access to sensitive systems, reviewing software permissions, replacing exposed credentials, and monitoring unusual account activity or large data transfers.

  • MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella confirmed several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft notes its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

Recent findings suggest that “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Organization to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

In a recent development, the approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft stated it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman remarked during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

It has been revealed that the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

According to recent reports, western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman noted of the upcoming coding model the tech giant confirmed at Ignite.

In a recent development, the tech giant also released its fresh image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Foelber – Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 6:45AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

It has been revealed that it has been a brutal month for Nvidia (NVDA +2.41%) investors. Concerns about sustained cash burn among hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet sparked a widespread sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, especially semiconductor stocks. Then matters got much, much worse.

In a recent development, on Nov. 8, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair that U.S. officials are looking into for potential national security concerns. After market close on Nov. 11, The Upcoming York Times reported that Huang had a different affair with an Nvidia employee. News of yet another affair with a separate employee surfaced on Nov. 12. That same day, Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO -- effective immediately -- with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia's CEO transition has market-rippling effects, given Huang has been CEO since the tech giant's founding 33 years ago and the sheer size of Nvidia and its impact on the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.33%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +0.77%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -1.64%). Few CEOs carry as much importance. The only comparable examples are fellow founders at large tech-focused companies like Elon Musk at Tesla and Space Exploration Technologies, Mark Zuckerberg at Meta Platforms, or long-tenured prominent CEOs like Hock Tan at Broadcom. But Huang takes the cake given the length of his tenure and Nvidia's valuation.

Huang's shoes are arguably too major to fill by one person alone. Here's why Kress' leadership now matters more than ever, even if she eventually passes the baton to a long-term CEO, and what that could mean for the stock going forward.

Sources indicate that colette Kress. Image source: Nvidia.

One of the most effective leadership dynamics is a visionary, borderline unbridled CEO with a bounty of massive ideas contrasted with a shrewd realist that possesses unique technical, financial, operating, or accounting skills. Examples include Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, with Jobs pushing big ideas and Tim Cook acting as Apple's master operator.

Or Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg, with Sandberg serving as chief operating officer of Meta Platforms from 2008 to 2022. Without Sandberg, there's a good argument that Meta Platforms wouldn't be the streamlined cash cow it is today.

My personal favorite example is Walt Disney’s eponymous founder and president and his brother, Roy O. Disney. Because Roy was so good at managing the organization's credit lines and financial obligations, Walt was free to take chances on risky endeavors, enough of which paid off to create an entertainment giant.

In all three examples, the visionary captured Wall Street's spotlight, but the savvy operator provided the glue that held the business together.

In many ways, Kress counterbalanced Huang's visionary bets with pragmatic financial discipline. I suspect she was a major catalyst behind Nvidia's massive dividend increases and stock buybacks. After all, it was her comments during Nvidia's GTC 2026 conference that fueled my prediction that Nvidia would make a substantial dividend increase in 2026 and then a second correct prediction that Nvidia would surpass Apple in stock buybacks and dividends.

According to recent reports, reports indicate that Kress may have helped Nvidia commit $105 billion in credit to OpenAI rather than $250 billion and that she questioned the looseness of Nvidia's lending practices toward start-ups and AI cloud providers like neoclouds. It remains to be seen how true these reports are. But if you've tuned into Nvidia's earnings calls and presentations over the years, it's fairly clear that Kress comes across as more of a straightforward, often dry but highly capable executive compared to Huang's promotional, arrogant, but undeniably brilliant persona. My guess is that Kress has done a fair share of checking and balancing Huang behind the scenes, far more than she has been given credit for.

NASDAQ · As of 9:33 AM ET 11/18/26.

It has been revealed that huang has been instrumental in accelerating the AI build-out beyond hyperscalers to neoclouds and AI start-ups through direct lending practices, as well as aims to partner with a consortium of financial institutions to offer $500 billion in AI infrastructure financing. The only problem is that many AI start-ups haven't yet shown they can consistently turn a profit -- especially high-profile neoclouds like Nebius Group and CoreWeave.

Recent findings suggest that under Kress, I predict Nvidia's role in the AI build-out becomes much more hands-off. Up to this point, Nvidia has basically been running around Silicon Valley, handing out jars of lighter fluid for start-ups to throw onto the raging AI infrastructure bonfire. Kress could favor a more financially disciplined approach that prioritizes high cash flows over risky bets. That could slow Nvidia's growth rate, but it could also lead to gradual compounding over time rather than a cyclical boom followed by a downturn. Nvidia will likely miss out on some major moonshot bets it would have cashed in on under Huang, but it could also avoid some costly mistakes. And in the end, this dynamic may appeal more to investors who are confident in AI adoption over the long term but feel that the pace of progress has been too hot and too fast.

It has been revealed that if Nvidia's growth slows but it retains its ultra-high margins, then it wouldn't be surprising if Nvidia continued to aggressively buy back stock and raised its dividend under Kress. Under that framework, Nvidia could transform from a high-octane growth stock into a balanced company tailor-made for value investors -- as Nvidia trades at just 19.7 times earnings and 16.7 times forward earnings estimates.

Risk-taking beats caution when the bets pay off, which they mostly have for Nvidia. So it's understandable why the stock is down as much as it is. But a less risky strategy could also make Nvidia far less vulnerable to an AI spending downturn.

I wouldn't be surprised if Kress plays an integral role in prolonging the AI boom by taking a slower and steadier approach rather than Huang's full-throttle innovative spirit. This approach could make Nvidia a lot more boring, but it could also pay off for long-term investors willing to endure this period of volatility.

Recent findings suggest that that said, Huang's sudden resignation has fundamentally challenged Nvidia's investment thesis. There's a ton of uncertainty as to how the company will perform under new management, whether it is caught flat-footed and loses market share and talent to competitors, and whether national security breaches will hinder Nvidia's ability to sell chips in China. For those reasons, I think it's totally fair for investors to hold Nvidia and keep it on a watch list until there's more clarity on where Nvidia could be headed from here.

GTA 6 Review: The Megayacht of Gaming Has Something for Nearly Everyone

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype.
  • GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage.
  • Sources indicate that environments that were sketched out in the last game, such as stores and buildings, are detailed and explorable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype. Expansive, interactive and peppered with so much to do that it’s easy to sink scores of hours into the launch game — and who knows how much more will be added later on.

GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage.

Sources indicate that environments that were sketched out in the last game, such as stores and buildings, are detailed and explorable. Bystanders and police react more naturally to your presence and culpability — cops now have to see you escaping the crime scene to tag you as a suspect for pursuit. You can talk people down from fights. And the game’s titular transgression of stealing cars is more nuanced than ever.

Granted, early versions of some of these advancements were explored in Rockstar’s interim game, 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, and the series iteratively progressed with all the updates that continue to this day for GTA Online, which was built out from GTA 5 to be an ever-evolving game-as-a-service. But they’ve been taken to the next level in GTA 6, leading to a world that feels more responsive to your presence and actions. With all its systems, map space and activities, it feels like the megayacht of gaming — a polished experience in all its corners, with some of the most detailed graphics you’ll find in gaming.

A lot of that rests on the shoulders of the game’s protagonists, lovers in crime Lucia and Jason, who operate radically differently from previous GTA point-of-view characters. Their romance (if players choose to pursue it) offers a whole new narrative and systematic view of a life outside the law, with collaborative and solo missions that paint a vivid picture of the playful, dangerous world of GTA. Outside story missions, casually driving around as a couple fills the dead air with conversation and the robberies with partnered backup, enriched by their growing relationship, lathering their activities with all the sweetness of a violent date night.

The couple’s story is a very lengthy affair — at 50 hours in, the game claims I’ve completed roughly 70% of it — and is robust enough to justify the price of entry. It’s a compelling narrative about two people trying to build a future through a dangerous world by leaning deeper into the danger, but it’s also a showcase of the world Rockstar built. After the story is done, the game hands you the keys to explore it yourself however you’d like.

In a recent development, rockstar declined to comment on whether GTA 6 will transition into the next version of GTA Online, but it feels like an inevitability. It’s hard to ignore the vast space, systems and mechanics that players only briefly dabble with while playing through the story. From fishing to treasure hunting in underwater shipwrecks to big game hunting to street racing, there’s a lot of low-stakes fodder to unwind with the game — and plenty of bank heists, chases and other random crimes to ratchet up the tension, too.

It has been revealed that at launch, GTA 6 has a broad foundation of things to do that — I suspect — will increase over time. It’s layered with Rockstar’s signature puerile humor, and I’ll fess up to laughing at some of the frequent boner jokes and crass names (one sportscar brand is the “pfister”), but the occasional homophobia and transphobia is bizarrely out of time — the game’s mock-everything culture still feels rooted in the 2000s, aimed at people who loved the edginess of South Park in its heyday. More modern satire appears in bystander conversations that range into absurd caricatures of far-right anti-woke crusaders and rabid leftists, but given the game’s faux-Florida setting in the fictional state of Leonida (which includes the legendary Vice City), there’s far more of the former than the latter.

Industry observers note that thus, the world feels textured even for players just picking up the game to fool around. While there are sparse stretches of the map, little side stories unfold for those who notice and follow strange things afoot. But a massive part of the game’s appeal and heart lies in the ballad of two lovebirds, kept apart by immaturity and circumstance but brought together through crime and the skewed American dream at the center of every GTA: Pull off a big enough heist and the world is yours.

Sources indicate that the game’s story opens from Jason’s perspective — a twentysomething guy, former military, quiet and gruff, drifting through life doing odd jobs for a small-time kingpin out in the sticks. A little drug-running and skirmishing with the local gangs keep him busy, working out and drinking beers on his deck, watching the sunset from GTA 6’s version of the Florida Keys.

All that changes when Lucia, who stole and then broke his heart, gets out of prison on early release and asks to crash with him during her parole. A tenuous second chance is complicated when she reconnects with a former cellmate who’s partnered with a rich hotshot dangling wealth in front of our fragile couple. This could be the ticket to a financial foundation to help them start anew. Then a job goes wrong, and the pair go on the run, restarting in a rural backwater as far from the clubs of Vice City as one can get.

This is where players decide how close they want Jason and Lucia to be. The game sets up the beginnings of their reconnection, but they can drift apart if players don’t choose to bring them closer. It’s all about the little things: Jason holding the door for Lucia, one of them buying clothes for the other at the vendor, or even just sidling close during morning coffee. Rockstar didn’t want to force players into this relationship — even if things fizzle, the pair will still go through the game as partners in crime, doing jobs together even if they sleep apart.

In a recent development, but players will value something if they have to work for it, Rob Nelson, head of development at Rockstar North, told me over a video call. He likened the couple’s relationship to how players embraced the honor system in RDR2, with more taking the high honor route than being a vicious criminal.

“When you can lose something, it’s more meaningful if you work to keep it,” Nelson stated.

As Nelson explained, Rockstar came off of GTA 5’s story with its three protagonists wondering how to one-up it for the sequel, which started development soon after in 2015 but took until early 2019 to settle on GTA 6’s main pair. A romantic couple is indeed a step up from characters who come together for a job and split after, and Rockstar had to figure out how that’s different for lovers — they’re not going to end a job at 2 a.m. and part ways; they’re going home to go to bed, Nelson said.

Recent findings suggest that the couple essentially have a run-on conversation that lasts through the story, piping up during long drives to chat about a recent mission or bring up something from their pasts. How much these topics are tailored to events and how much are randomly chosen feels cleverly obscured, coming off like the natural chatter between two people slowly figuring each other out. The sheer scale of the recorded dialogue dwarfs other games and becomes a feature among many, showcasing the titanic work Rockstar put into GTA 6.

Industry observers note that it all adds up to a compelling narrative centered on two characters, carefully chiseled to embody the best and worst of Vice City, inspired by the real-life Bonnie and Clyde and by crime couples from films like True Romance and Natural Born Killers. GTA 6’s couple starts with a meet-cute over trying to steal the same car, and freshly out of prison, Lucia eggs on Jason to take bigger illegal jobs than the small-time gigs he’s coasted on. Even with an ankle monitor and picking up road trash on work duty, Lucia never seriously considers staying on the right side of the law. Jason is cautious about new opportunities, but eager not to lose Lucia again, and never considers going straight.

Sources indicate that nestled within their stories is a serious point about the futility of staying honest in a city and system that caters to the rich and punishes the desperate. A flashback demonstrates Lucia juggling gig economy rideshare driving and having her utilities shut off after failed payments, which is heartbreakingly real. But it’s a blip amid the overwhelming focus on a criminal romance, where the only escape from poverty is to steal substantial bills until finally retiring to a distant island beyond the consequences of your felonious lifestyle.

It’s not surprising — that’s the GTA fantasy, after all — but it’s telling which things Rockstar took great pains to update to modern tastes over the game’s decade-plus development (and what it left out). Smartphones are a huge part of the game’s social interactions, from texting and calling contacts to Instagram-like social media feeds to summoning cars through an app or hailing a ride. But notably absent are any gig economy services that have normalized atypical incomes — you can’t TaskRabbit or Uber your way to an honest living in GTA 6. Odd jobs come as under-the-table favors you do for the rich and powerful, frequently taking advantage of both protagonists’ gray morals.

Though it won’t give you the option of a legal living, GTA 6 leans into the injustice of the wealth gap, putting a few city blocks between gang-riddled run-down apartments and the high-rise clubs populated by ignorant rich assholes. The game gleefully showcases the hypocrisy of the privileged — one time, I rushed into a rural, well-off house where a wife espousing family values ushered me to help her dying husband… who was choking in a BDSM leather harness. Once freed, he tucked his tail back into his submissive role as a “liberal cuck” for their roleplay.

This kind of edginess-for-laughs is peppered around the game, and it’s hard not to feel the cynicism. I can de-escalate some situations, but a lot of the non-player characters you run into on the street are on a hair-trigger eager to fight. You’ll overhear plenty of anti-immigrant screeds from random bystanders. Junkies try to break into your car if you have contraband in the trunk.

If GTA 5 was released in the waning Obama years with waning public optimism, GTA 6 launches halfway into Trump’s second term, where far-right government ICE deportations and street killings have polarized the nation beyond anything we’ve seen in decades. Yet when I asked how Rockstar had adjusted the game over its long development to suit this moment, Nelson mentioned that Jason and Lucia’s story is a counterweight of optimism and care amid all the crime and societal disparity in the game.

It has been revealed that “Choosing love is a bit of an act of rebellion against a narcissistic culture,” Nelson said. “The ideas of selfishness and selflessness put through this world is interesting to us, giving you goals other than just maxing out your bank account with supercars and properties.”.

Recent findings suggest that evaluating a game with so much detail spread across a vast map area is difficult, as the polish can be mistaken for quality. When I parked in a narrow driveway, I noticed Jason has an entire animation for shimmying through a slim gap. There have to be a dozen sequences for ways he and Lucia can sidle up to each other for a quick peck or embrace, all optional. There must be a thousand or more buildings you can duck into to explore their interiors. And the amount of dialogue feels unfathomably colossal, all voiced with aplomb by talented actors.

Where other games have some, GTA 6 has more. It’s a little like asking whether a megayacht is enjoyable to commute to work. The simple answer is yes, GTA 6 is an incredible game. And yet, its scope can be distracting. Halfway through the story, I was zipping from destroying drug dens to stealing valuable cars for a collector to hunting major game in the rural hills — all good fun, but my attention easily peeled away from the main story and the couple’s attempt to secure their financial independence, retire early future. The last chapter had ended in a gun battle as hired killers came for a dangerous MacGuffin in Jason and Lucia’s hands, but amid all the good, clean street crime, that danger had receded to the background.

Recent findings suggest that the story’s punch is diluted by everything you can and probably will do, which feels like forgetting the taste of the prime rib after sampling everything else at a buffet. But at least all those activities are enjoyable and round out the criminal with the casual, including mini golf and mud races far from the dense urban core of Vice City. It’s like if Lego Island grew up to add larceny to its roster of fun things to do.

It has been revealed that in grappling with the scale of the game, I repeatedly reach for simile — too many options make it harder to fully define GTA 6 and who it’s for, outside of saying there’s so much that its appeal spreads very wide. There’s not quite something for everyone, but it offers such a plethora of side activities that if one gets tiring, another will probably tide you over. This is what will most likely form the foundation of an eventual transition to GTA Online: A substantial stream of things to do on top of stacking cash. And given GTAO’s sustained success, the baseline version of GTA 6 will please all the heist junkies and freeform adventurers who’ve loved the series, even if they aren’t hooked by the well-crafted core story. All the looky-loos curious about the hype will find one of the most polished video games ever made.

Sources indicate that GTA fans will notice a lot of small improvements that clean up logical inconsistencies. Witnesses have to notice you doing a crime to report it, and cops have to see you flee a crime scene to put out an all-points bulletin on your description, though you can lower your chances of being recognized by swapping outfits and respraying the color of your getaway ride.

Other new features add complexity to the game. Certain crimes are riskier until you get new tools and connections unlocked through the story, which let you steal cars with trackers and rob banks with countermeasures. Exercise and diet affect your health and physique, which you’ll need to maintain with regular workouts. You can steal guns and vehicles, but they won’t be saved unless you pay to buy or register them, respectively.

According to recent reports, these sound tedious, but they’re little frictions that make living in the world of GTA 6 more intentional. Early in the game as Jason, I frequently found myself waking up in the morning, grabbing a cup of coffee and doing a workout to get my in-game day “started,” putting on the radio and feeding my snake or checking in with Lucia ambling around the kitchen. As the relationship between the two deepens, they can go to bed together, cuddled up and doomscrolling on their phones.

While I expect a million posts of “he just like me fr fr” to blanket social media as people wonder at the work Rockstar put in to replicate our (often terrible) habits, there’s still a lot I was delighted to discover that’s unique to the world they’ve made. Some of these are jokes taken to an extreme, like the intentionally pretentious game-within-a-game you can play, Tenebrae Lux — a black-and-white walking simulator by an in-universe auteur, Johannes Zuch, whose name flashes on the screen so many times that it feels like a wink toward Hideo Kojima and other famous game creators.

“We love auteurs — it’s not mocking, it’s celebrating,” Nelson mentioned.

In a recent development, but my favorite things in any GTA game are the side stories you can chance upon that are scripted but feel emergent, exploring the bizarre nooks and crannies of the world. One night halfway through the game, I was casually driving around as Lucia when I saw a police chopper aiming a spotlight at the street — and found the cops in a standoff with a man in a fox suit.

I immediately discovered that, in the game’s fictional state of Leonida, being a furry (e.g., wearing a fursuit and expressing your fursona) is illegal, so I broke through the police blockade to liberate him. I met up with his fellow furries and spirited them away to a compound, during which I peeked over my shoulder to find them nuzzling each other. God bless you little oddballs bravely living your truth in the face of unjust laws.

In a recent development, like its forebears, GTA 6 feels like two games — a core narrative about making a living through the underground in a rags-to-riches-to-rags-to-riches saga of a star-crossed couple, and a massive sandbox to do whatever you want. While going treasure hunting in offshore wrecks or making drug drop-offs from a plane dilutes the story’s tension, it also gives you a lot of opportunity to find the GTA you want to experience. After the story fades into memory, that’s what’ll stick around as the core of this game: the freedom to choose what you want to do, laws be damned.

Eventually, you’ll face that ultimate temptation to cause such havoc that you’ll trigger the game’s newly introduced, sixth star of police attention — one in which it feels like every cop in Leonida is coming after you, and it doesn’t stop until you’re arrested or put down, a countdown to how long Jason and Lucia can stick it to the law at maximum volume.

“I haven’t played six stars since we finalized it, I made it too long so we made it harder,” Nelson remarked. “I’m curious to see what times people get!”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

Recent findings suggest that but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

Sources indicate that I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is presently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

Recent findings suggest that this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

In a recent development, desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

With the repository added, you can install it with:.

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Did Avalanche’s New NYSE Deal Just Make Solana and XRP Irrelevant?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and its owner, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE +0.22%), just handed the cryptocurrency Avalanche (AVAX -2.48%) a central role in their plan to launch a new exchange for tokenized stocks.
  • According to recent reports, the NYSE deal immediately looks like bad news for two other cryptocurrencies that have been positioning themselves as the preferred solution for this exact niche.
  • Talking about the choice of Avalanche, NYSE executive Dennis Lee mentioned that the company wanted to pick a blockchain solution that offered predictable costs and strong control over the permissible participants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 18, 2026 at 6:50AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Avalanche ›.

Sources indicate that the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and its owner, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE +0.22%), just handed the cryptocurrency Avalanche (AVAX -2.48%) a central role in their plan to launch a new exchange for tokenized stocks. On Nov. 9, Ava Labs, Avalanche's developer, confirmed it would provide blockchain technology for a new NYSE-affiliated venue for those tokens. This is the best news that the coin's holders have gotten in recent memory, but its price was little changed for the seven days ended Nov. 13.

According to recent reports, the NYSE deal immediately looks like bad news for two other cryptocurrencies that have been positioning themselves as the preferred solution for this exact niche. Apparently, the NYSE was influenced by properties like Avalanche's speed, throughput, and regulatory tooling. Yet Solana (SOL -0.22%) is dramatically ahead of Avalanche on the first two, and XRP's (XRP +0.81%) network, the XRP Ledger (XRPL), has built strong compliance tools directly into its systems. So did Avalanche and the NYSE deal just make both of those coins irrelevant?

CRYPTO · As of 9:35 AM ET 11/18/26.

Talking about the choice of Avalanche, NYSE executive Dennis Lee mentioned that the company wanted to pick a blockchain solution that offered predictable costs and strong control over the permissible participants. It's also very likely that a major exchange launching a new venue would want to choose something with high throughput capacity and speed to handle the volume it could bring to the table.

Since its latest upgrade, Alpenglow, Solana finalizes transactions on its network in about 150 to 400 milliseconds. Avalanche takes about two full seconds, and the XRPL takes several seconds. In terms of transaction costs, Solana's median fee is $0.0004, whereas Avalanche's is $0.01, and the XRPL's is $0.00001. At first glance, it looks as if both Solana and the XRPL were passed over in favor of a more expensive (and in Solana's case, much slower) solution here.

Solana is also already home to a large sum of tokenized asset trading activity. It hosted $583 million in tokenized stocks as of Nov. 13, more than triple Avalanche's $179 million; the XRPL doesn't host any of those assets. So while it makes sense that the XRPL isn't a good fit for NYSE's needs, Solana still looks like a stronger option than what they actually went with on paper.

The XRP Ledger supports permissioned decentralized exchanges (DEXs), which are trading venues built into its blockchain that can be configured to admit only specific accounts holding approved credentials. That's a gated venue on a shared ledger, while the NYSE wanted a ledger of its own. One explanation for the NYSE's selection of Avalanche is that, per Ava Labs, the exchange will run its own custom blockchain built with Avalanche's technology, rather than settling on Avalanche's public chain. That fits the access control requirement.

CRYPTO · As of 9:47 AM ET 11/18/26.

So, Solana's and the XRPL's advantages mainly apply to their public ledgers, whose tokenized asset bases, transaction costs, and speed rankings mean little to a business looking to run its own private blockchain.

It has been revealed that realistically, Avalanche clinching the NYSE deal was a major missed opportunity for Solana and, to a lesser extent, XRP. But Solana holders should not be too hung up on that, as Solana landed a smaller win the same day.

Sources indicate that formation Securities told regulators on Nov. 9 that it aims to launch a upcoming tokenized stock venue of its own running on Solana's network in early 2027, specifically citing its speed, low costs, and its existing base of tokenized real-world assets — ownership rights of things like stocks and bonds converted into tradeable crypto. Its trades would post directly to Solana's public ledger, incurring standard fees.

Recent findings suggest that in contrast, Avalanche's NYSE deal will likely offer its coinholders little directly. So Solana lost some prestige here more than it lost potential revenue. XRP, for its part, just got fresh evidence that, somewhat surprisingly, its network's native compliance tooling is not as appealing to the institutions it's courting as what its developers and its investors may have hoped.

CRYPTO · As of 9:44 AM ET 11/18/26.

Sources indicate that more broadly, the risk here is that other exchanges will copy the NYSE's template, launching their own blockchain products within small, exclusive walled gardens rather than launching them on public blockchains. That could lead to more lost business and further diminish the institutional adoption thesis for buying Solana and XRP, among many other coins.

Still, don't sell Solana or XRP over this.

During the next few quarters, watch for fresh exchanges for tokenized assets to announce their aims to launch and their chosen crypto partners. If XRP doesn't net any of those deals, it will be a deeply bearish sign, and if Solana can't capture at least a couple more, it's an indication that its competitive environment is getting fiercer and harder to navigate successfully.
